verified_facts.fact: Google published the family-agent post with the byline date "Sep 17, 2026", by Tom Shane, Senior Product Manager, Google Labs.
Google's official RSS records this exact post's publish time as 18:15 UTC on 17 September 2026, which is 2026-09-18 02:15 in Taipei.
The standfirst states the change: an experimental agent built for families, aimed at reducing household logistics.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: Google Labs introduces a new experimental agent built for families, helping households spend less time on logistics and more time together.

verified_facts.fact: CC is not new on this date: Google states it originally launched CC as a personal agent, that it quickly became a daily habit for many early testers, and that in May it was brought into the Gemini App as Daily Brief.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: It quickly became a daily habit for many early testers and in May we brought it to the Gemini App as Daily Brief

verified_facts.fact: The core mechanical change: CC now has its own Google account, which Google says gives it a distinct identity and a clear permissions model, with up to six members able to manage and collaborate with it.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: It has its own Google account that gives CC a distinct identity and clear permissions model, enabling up to six members to manage and collaborate with the agent.

verified_facts.fact: The sharing boundary Google states: CC only sees what each member chooses to share, with examples of emails from a child's school, a local swim centre or the vet.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: CC only sees what each member chooses to share, such as emails from your child’s school, the local swim center, or the vet.

verified_facts.fact: The account is described as verified; Google states two limits: it only responds to group members, and will not act or share outside the group without permission.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: It only responds to group members, and will not take action or share information outside the group without your permission.

verified_facts.fact: Feature 1, the shared morning brief: each morning CC delivers a shared 'Your Day Ahead' brief covering who needs to be where, what needs doing, and what CC completed the previous day.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: Each morning, CC delivers a shared “Your Day Ahead” brief.

verified_facts.fact: Feature 2: CC tracks dates and to-dos and pulls shared information into a family Calendar or Task list, keeping them updated as things change.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: CC automatically tracks important dates and to-dos, pulling relevant shared information from across your group into a family Calendar or Task list, and helps keep them up to date even as things change.

verified_facts.fact: Feature 3, the one where CC acts rather than summarises: filling out permission slips or activity registration PDFs, creating school supply shopping lists, or drafting weekly meal plans, asking for missing details and updating group memory.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: CC can also help you complete time consuming logistical tasks involved in running a family, such as filling out permission slips or activity registration PDFs, creating school supply shopping lists, or crafting weekly meal plans.

verified_facts.fact: Google states the permission condition for that acting, in an image caption under the feature.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: CC can take action, like filling out forms, with your permission.

verified_facts.fact: Control 1, per-member sharing: each member chooses what to share and what to keep private, and can change it at any time.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: Each member can easily choose what to share with CC and what to keep private, and can make changes at any time.

verified_facts.fact: Control 2, standing rules by sender: a member can pick email senders always shared with CC going forward, and receives a private weekly list of new senders to choose from.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: Pick the email senders that you always want to share with CC going forward, like your kids’ school or travel bookings. Each week, you’ll also receive a private list of new email senders that you can choose to share with CC.

verified_facts.fact: Control 3, one-off sharing: a member can forward an email or text to CC, share a Drive folder or files with it, or add CC to a Calendar.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: You can also share a Drive folder or files with CC or add CC to a Calendar.

verified_facts.fact: What CC connects to and what it runs on: Gmail, Chat, Docs and Calendar; every CC runs on its own isolated cloud computer powered by Google's agentic harness Antigravity and the latest Gemini models (no version number given). The quote below is trimmed where Google's sentence continues into a link: the rendered sentence reads "... powered by Google's agentic harness, Antigravity, and the latest Gemini models.", with "Antigravity" linking to antigravity.google. Only the trimmed, link-free run is stored so the quote is a contiguous string on the rendered page as well as in a tag-stripped read; the article uses only the "isolated cloud computer" half and, per must_not_write, names neither Antigravity nor a Gemini version.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: Behind the scenes, every CC runs on its own isolated cloud computer powered by Google’s agentic harness

verified_facts.fact: Memory is split between household and individual: a go-to grocery list or favourite family restaurants for the household; dietary preferences or local timezones for one person.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: CC remembers what applies to the whole household (like your go-to grocery list or favorite family restaurants) versus what belongs to one person (like dietary preferences or local timezones).

verified_facts.fact: Availability, quoted with Google's own missing period after 'U.S': an early Labs experiment, web and mobile, people 18 or over, in the U.S, with a personal Google account.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: CC is an early experiment from Google Labs, available on web and mobile for people (18+) in the U.S with a personal Google account.

verified_facts.fact: Two entry paths, neither immediate: existing users get an upgrade email 'in the coming days'; new users join a waitlist.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: Existing users will receive an email in the coming days to upgrade their account and new users can join the waitlist

verified_facts.fact: CC's original launch is dated Dec 16, 2025 on Google's earlier post, described then as an experimental productivity agent built with Gemini connecting Gmail, Google Calendar, Google Drive and the wider web.
The original CC delivered the same 'Your Day Ahead' briefing, but to one person's inbox each morning -- what the 2026-09-17 change turns into a shared brief.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: delivering a “Your Day Ahead” briefing to your inbox every morning

verified_facts.fact: The two availability sentences do not match, and both are Google's own: December 2025 said early access in the U.S. and Canada, 18+, 'starting with Google AI Ultra and paid subscribers'; September 2026 says the U.S. only, 18+, 'with a personal Google account', naming no subscription at all.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: CC is an early Labs experiment, launching in early access today to Google consumer account users 18+ in the U.S. and Canada, starting with Google AI Ultra and paid subscribers.

verified_facts.fact: Daily Brief, the Gemini-app form of CC the post points to, carries its own rollout limit: rolling out to eligible users in select regions, with more users, languages and countries promised only as a hope.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: Daily Brief is currently rolling out to eligible users in select regions.

verified_facts.fact: Below the FAQ, the same Daily Brief page prints a fine-print eligibility line that is more specific than 'select regions': availability is US-only, English-only, and limited to people 18 and over. SCOPE, checked in the DOM on 2026-09-18 by the independent factcheck: the line is not attached to any single FAQ answer or to one feature. It sits alone in a page-level <div id="disclaimers"> block that follows the closing tags of the FAQ section and a spacer, as the last content inside <main> before the footer. The page it governs is https://gemini.google/overview/daily-brief/, whose whole subject is Daily Brief, so the line covers that page's Daily Brief and nothing wider; it says nothing about the family version of CC, which has its own availability sentence on blog.google. Note also that the line opens with 'Availability varies.', a hedge the first draft dropped. This line was not in the prior exploration pass's verified_facts and is added here after being read directly on today's re-fetch.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: Availability varies. US-only. English-only. 18+.

verified_facts.fact: Google describes what Daily Brief does in the Gemini app: scanning inbox, calendar and tasks to serve a prioritised morning summary.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: Allow Gemini to dig through your digital clutter and scan your inbox, calendar, and tasks at hand.

verified_facts.fact: blog.google's official RSS is live and current: 20 <item> entries, the newest published 'Thu, 17 Sep 2026 20:00:00 +0000', confirming the feed is not stale.

not_said: Taiwan is not included, by omission and by the shape of the one sentence that states availability: it names exactly one country, the U.S. The article states that Google's stated availability is the U.S. only and does not say CC will or will not come to Taiwan -- Google gives no expansion plan, timeline or country roadmap for the family version anywhere in the post.

No price, and no statement about whether a Google AI subscription is required now. The September post names only 'a personal Google account'; the December 2025 post named Google AI Ultra and paid subscribers. Google never says the requirement changed, so the article reports both sentences with their dates and does not declare CC free.
No language scope for the family version. The post names no interface language and does not say whether CC works in Traditional Chinese or any language other than English.
No date for the upgrade emails beyond 'in the coming days', and no waitlist length, acceptance criteria or wait-time estimate.

No statement about children. The product is framed as being for families, with school forms and children's activities as examples, but the eligibility line is 18+, so a child cannot be one of the six members by Google's own rule; Google does not address this tension.
No data-handling detail: where shared email content is stored, how long it is kept, whether it is used to improve Google's models, or how a member removes something they previously shared.
No statement about what happens when a member leaves the group, when shared memory is deleted, or who owns CC's Google account.

No accuracy or error-handling detail: no statement about what happens if CC fills a form wrongly, books the wrong time or misreads an email, and no review mechanism described beyond the general 'with your permission'.
No usage limits, quotas or caps of any kind.
No independent testing -- every capability in this record is Google's own description; this site has run no test of CC (it is US-only).
No explanation of what Antigravity is beyond 'Google's agentic harness', and no version number tied to 'the latest Gemini models'.

editorial_brief:
Written for a Taiwanese general reader who cannot use CC today -- it is US-only -- but who runs a household where school notices land in one parent's inbox and clinic reminders in another's. The piece is worth their time because Google's design choices here (an agent with its own account, a hard cap of six members, per-member and per-sender sharing, a memory split between household and individual) are a concrete, published answer to a question that will keep recurring as more shared assistants appear: when one AI agent serves several people, whose information does it hold and who decides what it sees.

The two facts the piece is built around: (1) the printed date is Sep 17, 2026, but the RSS-confirmed publish time (18:15 UTC) is already Sep 18 in Taipei -- both dates are stated plainly near the top so a reader checking Google's own page is not confused; (2) Google names exactly one country, the U.S., for the family version, and separately never confirms or denies whether the Google AI Ultra / paid-subscriber condition from CC's December 2025 launch still applies -- both are reported with their own dates rather than resolved.

Structure used: two opening paragraphs (event + fact-check scope) and five sections -- what was announced and the date subtlety; the three things CC does for a household, closed by a table; the account/sharing/memory design, closed by the diagram; the conditions a reader must not skip (US-only, 18+, the subscription tension, the waitlist/email timing, and the 18+-versus-family-framing tension Google never addresses); and what Google has not said, plus a short, non-duplicating pointer to the Gemini app's own Daily Brief and its separate 'select regions' / 'US-only, English-only, 18+' limit.

Second closing link: the assignment names ai-news-google-assistant-gemini-20260904 ('Google Assistant 退場、Gemini 接手...') as the required second link, not ai-news-gemini-spark-20260519 that an earlier exploration pass had flagged as the natural pairing (since this post itself says CC became Daily Brief in the Gemini app in May). Both are legitimate neighbours -- one is the direct lineage of the underlying agent, the other is Google's other September assistant-transition story -- and the assignment's choice was followed; the divergence is noted in the report to the coordinator rather than silently substituted. Either way, this article does not re-teach what either neighbouring piece already covers: not Gemini Spark's automation-tier and authorisation mechanics, and not the Assistant-to-Gemini device handover.

Deliberately out of scope: how background agents decide what to automate (already covered 2026-05-19); anything from the AI-generated summary panel; any Gemini version number; comparisons with Apple, Amazon or any other household assistant (Google makes none); any hands-on impression, since this site has not used CC.
must_not_write: Do not write that Taiwanese users can use CC. Google's availability sentence names the U.S. only.
Do not write that CC will come to Taiwan, or that it will not. Google publishes no expansion plan for the family version.

Do not write that CC is free or that no subscription is needed. Report both Google sentences -- 'a personal Google account' (Sep 17, 2026) and 'Google AI Ultra and paid subscribers' (Dec 16, 2025) -- with their dates, and say Google has not stated whether the requirement changed.

Do not quote or paraphrase anything from the 'Read AI-generated summary' panel; it is machine-generated, carries Google's own experimental disclaimer, and contradicts the body on when a user can start.
Do not cite labs.google/cc for anything; its readable text is two words.
Do not say a child can join the group. The eligibility line is 18+, and Google does not explain how that fits the family framing.
Do not name a Gemini model version. Google wrote 'the latest Gemini models' with no number.
Do not date 'in May' to a specific day, and do not import ai-news-gemini-spark-20260519's 2026-05-19 date into a quote taken from this post.
Do not say CC acts autonomously; Google's own captions attach 'with your permission' to the acting features.
Do not write that this site tried or tested CC; it has not, and cannot -- it is US-only.
Do not re-explain in full what Daily Brief or Gemini Spark does; that belongs to ai-news-gemini-spark-20260519. One short paragraph of context is enough here.
Do not draw any logo, wordmark, UI screenshot or product icon in the diagram, and do not put a number in the diagram that is not also in the article body.

factcheck.checked_by: 獨立查核代理（未參與撰稿）
factcheck.method: sources[] 四條全部以 curl -sL -A "Mokaair-editorial" --max-time 90 重抓、剝掉 script/style/標籤後讀完 body（任何請求的 UA、標頭、查詢字串都沒有放入 email、姓名或個人資料）。四條的位元組數與撰稿紀錄完全相同：cc-expanding-to-groups 200／373,855、cc-ai-agent 200／388,980、gemini.google/overview/daily-brief 200／152,234、blog.google/rss 200／30,544。RSS 用 XML 解析而非字串比對，逐個 <item> 取 link 與 pubDate，確認本篇為 Thu, 17 Sep 2026 18:15:00 +0000、全 feed 20 則、最新一則 20:00:00 +0000。研究紀錄的 25 條 verbatim_quote 以 NFKC 正規化後做連續字串比對，25 條全部命中且 url 都在 sources[] 內。gemini.google 那行細則另外回到原始 HTML 看 DOM 位置以確認適用範圍。沒有使用任何 sources[] 以外的新網址替文章補事實。
factcheck.verdict: needs_second_round（依規格第 3 節：事實層面的修改超過十處。骨幹論述沒有動——美國限定、自己的帳號、每人各自決定分享、記憶分兩層、訂閱門檻不下結論，五件事都維持原樣；需要第二輪的是逐句回查本輪新寫進去的句子）
edits_to_the_pack: 第一段刪掉「這個帳號不屬於任何一位成員」：公告只寫 "It has its own Google account that gives CC a distinct identity and clear permissions model"，從來沒有說這個帳號不屬於任何成員；本篇第五節自己也寫「沒有寫這個帳號本身算是屬於誰的」，前後矛盾。已改成官方原話的「官方說這讓 CC 有獨立的身分與清楚的權限範圍」。
第 1 節第 2 段與 FAQ 第 5 題把引號裡的「今年 5 月」改成「5 月」，並加上「沒有印出年份」：公告寫的是 "in May we brought it to the Gemini App as Daily Brief"，年份是上下文推出來的，不是 Google 印的。把「今年」放進引號等於把一個來源沒寫的字算在 Google 頭上。
第 5 節第 3 段刪掉開頭的「如果只是想找現在就能用的版本」：Daily Brief 的細則是 US-only、English-only，台灣讀者並不能用，這句話會讓讀者以為有一個現在就能用的替代品。改寫後明講「台灣的使用者同樣用不到」，並補回細則開頭被漏掉的對沖詞 "Availability varies."（供應情況不一），同時寫出那一行的適用範圍是整個 Daily Brief 頁面。
表格第一列的「台灣帳號收不收得到未寫明」改成「未寫明可用的語言」：官方的開放條件已經寫明只有美國，說台灣收不收得到「未寫明」會讓讀者以為台灣可能在範圍內。語言則是公告真的沒有寫的東西（第 4 節第 1 段同步補上「或可用的語言」）。
表格第一、二列「需要誰同意」欄的「不用，屬於摘要通知」「不用，屬於整理與追蹤」改掉：公告只在會採取行動的功能上寫 "with your permission"，從來沒有說摘要與整理不需要同意；而且同意其實發生在更前面的分享設定。已改成「事前由各成員決定分享哪些內容」與「同上，只用成員分享出來的資訊」。
第 2 節第 2 段補回兩個被刪掉的限定：原文是 "pulling relevant shared information from across your group"，草稿寫成「散落在群組裡各個成員手上的相關資訊」，掉了 shared，會讀成 CC 看得到成員手上的全部資訊；原文的 "helps keep them up to date" 被寫成「持續更新」，也已改回「協助保持更新」。
第 2 節第 3 段「代替家人處理一些耗時的行政工作」改成「官方寫的是協助你完成」：原文是 "CC can also help you complete time consuming logistical tasks"，help you complete 不等於代替。同段補上歸因與 "activity registration PDFs" 的 PDF。
第 3 節第 1 段刪掉「在群組的信件或訊息串裡，CC 是用自己的帳號出現，就像另一位成員一樣，而不是借用某個人的帳號」：公告只寫 "This is how CC will show up when it interacts with the group"，沒有說信件或訊息串、沒有說像另一位成員、也沒有說不是借用誰的帳號。已改成貼著原文的「CC 在跟群組互動時就是用這個帳號現身」。
